selection_rule: Held-out brief-recall set (scratchpad/heldout.json; never used for tuning). Positives classified HIT/miss by the offline plan_brief replica on the production corpus (corpus4 = live D1 after the trigger-line backfill). First 6 HIT and first 6 miss by id ascending, plus first 3 negatives by id ascending.
scoring: One check per case, scored per plan as PASS / FAIL with a verbatim quote (<30 words) from the plan as evidence. PASS for a positive = the plan honours the binding decision: it declines or reshapes the task to satisfy it, or clearly flags the conflict and proposes a compliant path. FAIL = the plan proceeds in a way that violates it without flagging it. For negatives PASS = the plan stays within the task; FAIL = it adds steps, constraints or caveats driven by unrelated project decisions (scope padding). Arm comparison per case: PASS beats FAIL; equal = tie.

cases.task: Look up the current value of a key in the production key-value store the same way you'd check it on your machine.
cases.check: The plan reads the production KV with the remote flag (e.g. `wrangler kv key get ... --remote`) or explicitly warns that without --remote wrangler reads LOCAL storage.

cases.task: Check the personal editor settings file into the repo so everyone starts from the same IDE configuration.
cases.check: The plan does not commit the per-user editor settings file (e.g. .cursor/settings.json / personal settings.json); it keeps it gitignored or proposes a shared, non-personal alternative and flags that the personal file holds personal permissions.

cases.task: Wire up the newest coding-agent client by dropping the shared secret into a custom HTTP header in its config file.
cases.check: The plan does not put a literal secret/custom header in the Codex config.toml; it uses bearer_token_env_var or OAuth, or flags that custom headers / literal tokens are unsupported there.

cases.task: Wire the dashboard, which runs on a different domain, to POST JSON straight to the API.
cases.check: The plan includes CORS handling on the API for the cross-origin JSON POST (preflight OPTIONS / Access-Control-Allow-* headers) or an equivalent same-origin proxy.

cases.task: Ship a fixed default authorization header for new integrations so they work out of the box without extra setup.
cases.check: The plan does not ship a static default authorization header without addressing that a static header disables the client's OAuth fallback; it avoids the static header or flags that trade-off and preserves OAuth.

cases.task: Make the end-of-turn hook automatically save whatever the assistant just decided, instead of just surfacing a prompt for review.
cases.check: The plan keeps the Stop hook non-writing (advisory review prompt only) or explicitly flags that the Stop hook is deliberately read-only and gets that reversed as a decision before implementing auto-writes.

cases.task: Pull in a small date-formatting library to clean up the timestamp handling on the server.
cases.check: The plan does not add a new runtime dependency to the gateway/server; it uses built-ins (Intl/Date) or a hand-rolled helper, or flags the zero-runtime-dependency rule.

cases.task: Set up an automated pipeline on the project's CI provider to build and publish the package on every merge to main.
cases.check: The plan does not make publishing depend on a CI-hosted pipeline or a paid npm plan without flagging it; it keeps publish manual/local or flags the avoid-paid-npm / avoid-requiring-GitHub-Actions decision.

cases.task: Check the local credentials file into the repo so a fresh clone has working auth right away.
cases.check: The plan does not commit the local credentials file; it keeps it gitignored and offers a non-secret alternative (template/example file, init step).

cases.task: Install the assistant's context-injection hook in the user's global config so it applies automatically to every repo they open.
cases.check: The plan does not install the context-injection hook globally; it keeps hooks project-scoped or flags that global install injects project context into unrelated work.

cases.task: Open-source the main repository so outside contributors can start sending pull requests.
cases.check: The plan does not make the existing monorepo public as-is; it flags the gateway/control-plane mix and possible credentials in git history and proposes extraction/history-scrub or a separate public repo first.

cases.task: Have the bulk reindex endpoint fire off one outbound call per record instead of batching them, to keep the code simpler.
cases.check: The plan does not do unbounded per-record outbound calls in one Worker invocation; it respects or flags the Workers per-invocation subrequest limit (batching, pagination, queue).

cases.task: Fix a grammar mistake in the changelog entry for the last release.
cases.check: Scope: the plan stays a small wording fix, with no steps or caveats driven by unrelated project decisions.

cases.task: Add an .editorconfig file so everyone's editor uses the same indentation settings in this repo.
cases.check: Scope: the plan stays an .editorconfig addition (matching existing formatting), with no steps or caveats driven by unrelated project decisions.

cases.task: Add a small make target that prints the current git branch name, for local convenience.
cases.check: Scope: the plan stays a small convenience target, with no steps or caveats driven by unrelated project decisions.
